issues.t: Dual-clutch transmission jerks or hesitates at low speed
issues.sym: The car lurches, shudders or hesitates when pulling away, creeping in traffic or parking, and shifts can feel abrupt in stop-and-go driving.
issues.why: The 7-speed dual-clutch automatic uses computer-controlled clutches instead of a torque converter. Early software made low-speed engagement rough, and Mercedes released transmission control software updates. On higher-mileage cars the clutch packs themselves can wear.
issues.next: Ask a Mercedes dealer to check for and install the latest transmission software and to run a clutch adaptation. If the shudder persists after that, have the clutches and fluid inspected before it gets worse.

issues.t: Transmission won't shift into reverse
issues.sym: You select R but the car won't go into reverse, sometimes with a 'Gear change to R not possible' message. In some cases the even-numbered gears stop working too.
issues.why: Mercedes issued bulletins for these cars where a transmission fault blocks reverse and stores a fault code. The fix is usually transmission control software, but sometimes a part inside the dual-clutch unit is replaced.
issues.next: Don't keep cycling the shifter in traffic. Have the car scanned at a dealer and ask about the reverse-gear bulletins for the A220.

issues.t: Transmission slips into neutral after coasting in Eco mode
issues.sym: After the car coasts with the engine idling (the 'gliding' feature in Eco mode), the transmission stays in neutral instead of re-engaging a gear when you press the gas.
issues.why: A software problem in the transmission control unit could leave the gearbox in neutral when leaving gliding mode. Mercedes released a software update for it.
issues.next: Until it's fixed, use Comfort or Sport mode, which don't glide. Ask the dealer for the transmission software update.

issues.t: Fuel rail or injectors can leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: You may smell raw gasoline around the car or see fuel dampness near the top of the engine. Many cars show no sign at all before the recall repair.
issues.why: Small particles left between the fuel rail and the injectors during manufacturing can keep the seals from sealing, so fuel can leak onto a hot engine and start a fire.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't drive the car; have it towed. Check your VIN for recall 21V-961 and have the dealer replace the fuel rail and injectors for free.

issues.t: Front axle carrier can corrode and fail (recall)
issues.sym: Usually there is no warning. Severe corrosion could cause clunks, wandering steering or a sudden loss of steering control.
issues.why: The carrier (subframe) that holds the front suspension and steering can corrode and lose strength.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-990. The dealer will inspect the front axle carrier and replace it free if needed.

issues.t: Coolant leak and low-coolant warning
issues.sym: A low-coolant warning appears, the coolant level keeps dropping, or you notice a sweet smell after driving, often without a visible puddle.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a bulletin for coolant warnings caused by a leaking coolant line on these cars, and the 2.0L turbo engine is known for slow coolant seepage.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and don't drive if the engine overheats. Have the cooling system pressure-tested to find the leak; ask about the coolant line bulletin.

issues.t: Fuel smell from leaking fuel supply hose
issues.sym: You notice a raw gasoline smell, especially after a fill-up or when the car is parked in a garage.
issues.why: The fuel supply hose on these cars can leak. Mercedes extended the warranty coverage on that hose.
issues.next: Fuel leaks are a fire risk, so get it checked promptly. Ask a Mercedes dealer whether your car is covered by the fuel supply hose warranty extension.

issues.t: Car won't unlock or start with 'Battery - Start Engine' message
issues.sym: The keyless entry doesn't work, the car won't start, or a 'Battery - Start Engine' message appears, often after the car has sat for a day or more.
issues.why: Mercedes traced this to a control unit keeping the car's data network awake, which slowly drains the 12-volt battery. Always-on modules can cause similar drain.
issues.next: Use the emergency key to get in and jump-start or charge the battery. Then have a dealer test the battery and check for the bulletin and software fix.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves
issues.sym: A rough idle, hesitation when accelerating, misfires or slowly worsening fuel economy, usually at higher mileage.
issues.why: The 2.0L turbo engine injects fuel straight into the cylinders, so nothing washes the backs of the intake valves. Oil vapor bakes onto them over time.
issues.next: Have misfire codes checked. If carbon is the cause, a walnut-blast cleaning restores performance; it's often recommended every 60,000–80,000 miles.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil seepage
issues.sym: Oil residue around the top of the engine, a burning-oil smell after driving, or slowly dropping oil level.
issues.why: The rubber valve cover gasket hardens with heat and age and starts to seep oil, mostly at higher mileage.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the oil level. Have the leak confirmed and the gasket replaced before oil drips onto hot exhaust parts.

issues.t: Driver door lock switch can corrode, risking rollaway (recall)
issues.sym: The car may not realize the driver's door is open, so the automatic parking brake or auto-park feature may not engage when you get out.
issues.why: A small switch inside the driver's door lock can corrode and stop reporting that the door is open.
issues.next: Always put the car in Park and set the parking brake before getting out. Check your VIN for recall 26V-481; the dealer will replace the door lock free.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not be properly bolted (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms. In some cases the airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: The driver's front airbag module may not have been secured correctly at the factory, so it may not deploy properly in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-685. The dealer will inspect the airbag module and replace it free if needed.

issues.t: Brake pedal plate can bend (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal may feel different or move oddly, though most cars show no signs.
issues.why: Poor welding on the brake pedal can let its mounting plate bend, which can affect braking.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-314. The dealer will inspect the pedal welds and replace the pedal free if needed.

issues.t: Water in the footwells from A/C drain hose (recall)
issues.sym: Wet carpets in the front footwells or center tunnel, a musty smell, or electrical glitches after using the A/C.
issues.why: The A/C condensation drain hose may have been installed wrong, so water drips into the cabin instead of under the car and can damage electrical parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-416. The dealer will inspect and correct the drain hose free; ask them to dry the carpet and check for water damage.

issues.t: Rearview camera image doesn't show (recall)
issues.sym: The center screen goes black or reboots, and the backup camera picture doesn't appear when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Errors in the camera and MBUX multimedia software can leave the display blank or restart it.
issues.next: Look over your shoulder and use mirrors when backing up. Check your VIN for recalls 21V-354 and 22V-232; the fix is a free software update.

issues.t: Emergency call (eCall) may not work (recall)
issues.sym: An 'SOS not available' type message, or no symptoms at all. After a crash, the automatic emergency call may fail or send the wrong location.
issues.why: Software faults in the communication module and its SIM card can disable the emergency call system or report a wrong location.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 22V-365 and 21V-058. The fix is a free software update, done over the air or at a dealer.

issues.t: LED headlights misaimed after repair (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights seem to point too low, too high or to the side, giving poor night visibility or blinding other drivers.
issues.why: On some cars the LED headlights were adjusted incorrectly during an earlier repair.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-509. The dealer will replace the LED headlights free.

issues.t: Headlights aimed incorrectly (recall)
issues.sym: The headlight beam may not light the road properly or may glare at oncoming drivers.
issues.why: The headlights on some cars were not adjusted correctly at the factory.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-662. The dealer will check and correct the headlight aim free.

issues.t: Missing rear brake pad wear gauge (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. You just may not have the tool or instructions to check rear pad thickness yourself.
issues.why: The rear brake pad inspection gauge and its owner's manual instructions may be missing, which breaks a federal brake rule.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-732. The dealer will supply the gauge and manual information free.

issues.t: Rear child seat anchor may be missing a bar (recall)
issues.sym: A child seat may not latch firmly into the right rear seat's ISOFIX/LATCH anchors.
issues.why: The right rear ISOFIX bracket may be missing its right-side anchor bar, so a child seat can't be secured properly.
issues.next: Don't use LATCH in that seat until it's checked; use the seat belt to install the child seat. Check your VIN for recall 21V-034.

issues.t: Creaking or grinding from steering column
issues.sym: Creaking, squeaking, humming or grinding when you turn the steering wheel, especially at low speed.
issues.why: Mercedes has several bulletins for noises between the steering wheel and the switch module and from the steering column itself; the cause isn't always clear.
issues.next: It isn't usually a safety issue, but have the dealer check it against the steering noise bulletins, ideally while under warranty.

issues.t: Steering vibration when parking or at low speed
issues.sym: The steering wheel vibrates or shudders when parking, turning slowly or driving under about 30 mph.
issues.why: Mercedes bulletins link this to the electric power steering software, and in some cases to tire changes.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for the electric power steering software update and look at tire balance.

issues.t: Front brakes squeal when stopping
issues.sym: A high-pitched squeal from the front brakes as you come to a stop.
issues.why: Mercedes acknowledged front brake squeal in a bulletin and says braking power isn't affected.
issues.next: Make sure the pads aren't worn out. If they're fine, ask the dealer about the brake squeal bulletin.

issues.t: Chirping or tapping from engine pulley when cold
issues.sym: A chirp or light tapping from the front of the engine on a cold start that often fades as the engine warms up.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a bulletin for noise near the crankshaft pulley on cold engines.
issues.next: Have a shop listen to it to rule out a worn belt or tensioner, and mention the bulletin.

issues.t: Humming or vibration from rear axle when maneuvering
issues.sym: Humming or vibration from the rear of the car when parking, turning tightly or pulling away on all-wheel-drive (4MATIC) models.
issues.why: Mercedes issued bulletins about rear axle humming and about faults in the all-wheel-drive control unit on these cars.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the rear drive unit and its software against the 4MATIC bulletins.

issues.t: Squeak or rattle from exhaust flap
issues.sym: A squeak or rattle from the back of the car, especially on start-up or when the exhaust valve opens and closes.
issues.why: The electrically operated exhaust flap valve can squeak or fail. Mercedes issued a bulletin and extended warranty coverage on the exhaust valve system.
issues.next: Ask a Mercedes dealer whether the exhaust valve warranty extension covers your car.

issues.t: Check engine light from fuel pump control software
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: Software in the fuel pump control module can store false sensor faults. Mercedes extended emissions warranty coverage for that module's software.
issues.next: Have the codes read at a dealer and ask about the fuel system control module software update.

issues.t: Side windows squeak or stick when moving
issues.sym: Windows go up and down slowly or with resistance, cracking or squeaking.
issues.why: Mercedes linked this to the inner window sealing rail.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect the window seals under the bulletin.

issues.t: MBUX screen freezes, goes dark or reboots
issues.sym: The central screen or driver display goes black, freezes, restarts by itself, or voice control stops working.
issues.why: MBUX multimedia software bugs; Mercedes has released many fixes through dealer and over-the-air updates.
issues.next: Make sure all over-the-air updates are installed. If it keeps happening, ask the dealer to update the head unit software.

issues.t: Water leak from panoramic sunroof drains
issues.sym: Wet headliner, damp carpet or water dripping inside after rain or a car wash; the roof may also creak.
issues.why: The sunroof's drain tubes clog with debris, so water overflows into the cabin.
issues.next: Have the drains cleared and the roof inspected before water damages electronics.

issues.t: Front control arm bushings and ball joints wear
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, vague steering or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Rubber bushings and ball joints in the front suspension wear, especially on rough roads.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected and get an alignment after any repair.
